- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

──────────────────────── PROMPT FOR A NEW SESSION ─────────────────────────
DISCLAIMER: Claude wrote this prompt. Examine it for inconsistencies and
verify its claims yourself — do not follow it blindly. Every fact below was
read off git, not the GitHub API, and the API may say something different.
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Investigate why five Claudinite members stopped converging around 10 August
2026 and have not landed a mount update since, despite running the converge
successfully every day.

## The affected members

missingbulb/CrosswordChat, missingbulb/EdFringeNow,
missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator, missingbulb/LaughCounter,
missingbulb/TLDR

## Evidence gathered (read from git only — no API access to these repos yet)

For all five, from `.claudinite-checks.json` at HEAD:

  maintenance.delivery   auto-merge            (nothing waits on a human)
  claudinite.ref         631a067f              IDENTICAL across all five
  claudinite.updated     2026-08-10 .. 08-12
  packVersions           no `claudinite-growth` key at all
                         (LaughCounter still shows the pre-date-anchored "7")

And from the remotes:

  last commit on main    2026-08-21   — the repos are live
  newest update branch   claudinite/update-2026-08-21-*  — created TODAY
  open claudinite/*      3, 8, 10, 17 and 51 branches respectively

So the scheduler runs, the converge runs, it produces an update branch every
day, and the branch never merges. The open-branch count is one per attempt,
accumulating since roughly 10 August. The identical pinned ref across all
five is the strongest signal: they all stopped advancing at the same canon
ref at the same time.

Two members on the same fleet — missingbulb/VascularColoring and
missingbulb/ShoutsAndWhispers — DID converge today and are at the current
pack versions, so this is a subset, not the whole fleet. Working out what
separates the five from those two is probably the fastest route to the cause.

Three more members (ClaudiniteWebsite, MissingBulbWebsite, WIP) could not be
read at all from this session and are unknown, not healthy — check them too.

## Why it matters

It blocks the last open box on missingbulb/Claudinite#1158: every folding
member's usage file should read `"version": 3`. These five still read v2
because they never received the claudinite-growth pack version that folds v3.
Readers accept v2, so nothing is broken for a user — but the members are ~10
days behind on everything the canon has shipped, not just this.

## How to proceed

1. Attach the five repos to the session (`add_repo`, access "push"), then
   read, for each: the open `claudinite/update-*` PRs, and the head sha's
   `pull_request` check runs.
2. There is a standing rule in the canon that applies directly here:
   "Diagnosing a member's maintenance PR that won't land — `unstable` beside
   a green sweep is a parked `action_required` run, not a missing repo
   setting. Read the member's raw .claudinite-checks.json and the head sha's
   pull_request runs; propose a platform-settings change only as a
   conclusion, never as a diagnosis." Do not open with a settings theory.
3. A likely-looking hypothesis worth testing early, but NOT assuming: a
   branch-protection or Actions-permissions change around 10 August that
   auto-merge cannot satisfy. Confirm it against a real run before saying it.
4. Whatever the cause, the backlog of up to 51 stale update branches per repo
   needs a cleanup plan — but assess branches read-only and act only on
   issues, per the tidy-repo policy.

## Useful mechanics discovered this session

- `api.github.com` IS reachable from the shell with an Authorization header
  when the proxy is injecting a credential, but the injection can be lost on
  a container restart (`GITHUB_TOKEN` reads literally as "[REDACTED:env:GH_TOKEN]",
  and requests come back 401/403). Check with:
      curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" https://api.github.com/user
  If that is not 200, use the GitHub MCP tools instead.
- The git proxy serves PUBLIC repos with no attachment at all, and is much
  cheaper than the MCP file reads (which return whole files). To read one
  file from many repos:
      git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --no-checkout -q \
        https://github.com/missingbulb/<REPO> <REPO>
      git -C <REPO> show HEAD:.claudinite-checks.json
  Private repos fail this and do need attaching.
- Node's `fetch` does not honour HTTPS_PROXY by default, so the vendored
  engine scripts 401 when run from a session. `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 node …`
  fixes it (Node 22 — the EnvHttpProxyAgent warning is expected).

## Deliverable

A root cause named with the evidence for it, and either the fix applied or a
tracking issue in missingbulb/Claudinite stating what a human must change and
where. Link it back to #1158.
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

  newest update branch   claudinite/update-2026-08-21-*  — created TODAY
  open claudinite/*      3, 8, 10, 17 and 51 branches respectively

day, and the branch never merges. The open-branch count is one per attempt,
accumulating since roughly 10 August. The identical pinned ref across all
five is the strongest signal: they all stopped advancing at the same canon
ref at the same time.

Two members on the same fleet — missingbulb/VascularColoring and
missingbulb/ShoutsAndWhispers — DID converge today and are at the current
pack versions, so this is a subset, not the whole fleet. Working out what
separates the five from those two is probably the fastest route to the cause.

read at all from this session and are unknown, not healthy — check them too.

It blocks the last open box on missingbulb/Claudinite#1158: every folding
member's usage file should read `"version": 3`. These five still read v2
because they never received the claudinite-growth pack version that folds v3.
Readers accept v2, so nothing is broken for a user — but the members are ~10
days behind on everything the canon has shipped, not just this.

1. Attach the five repos to the session (`add_repo`, access "push"), then
   read, for each: the open `claudinite/update-*` PRs, and the head sha's
   `pull_request` check runs.
2. There is a standing rule in the canon that applies directly here:

   a green sweep is a parked `action_required` run, not a missing repo
   setting. Read the member's raw .claudinite-checks.json and the head sha's
   pull_request runs; propose a platform-settings change only as a

{"number":1158,"title":"claudinite-dashboard: usage-backed data plane, per-repo redesign, repo/fleet modes — and retire fleet-usage","body":"Tracking issue for the dashboard redesign. The plan below is ordered by what blocks (out-of-band setup → one review pass over a PR stack → unattended execution → destructive tail), not by subject. Once agreed, this body is append-only.

## First, the question asked: is `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` redundant?

**Yes — with one catch that sequences the removal.**

- The sweep is a **stateless full recompute, a pure function of the members' current files** (its own README says so). It holds **no longer history** than the members: each member's week rows are append-once and never pruned, so the member files are the complete record and the fleet file adds no depth.
- **Nothing in the canon reads it.** Grep finds only the task's own files, its tests, docs and the `.gitattributes` entry. It was built for fleet-wide analysis by a human/agent reading one file — the fleet dashboard is now that reader, better.
- The **access argument is real and favors dropping**: the aggregate in Shepherd shows anyone with Shepherd read the whole fleet's numbers, while the dashboard reads each member's file *as the viewer* — a repo you can't read renders "not visible to you". Per-repo files are the permission-correct source.
- **Catch 1 — it is currently the fleet dashboard's roster.** Shepherd's declaration reads `"rosterFile": "usage-fleet.GENERATED.json"`. The member list is the one thing genuinely fleet-shaped in it, so the fleet page needs a replacement roster source *before* the file goes (PR 3 below).
- Catch 2 — the `coverage` census (absent / dormant / out-of-scope, with reasons) is the only other content member files can't hold. The fleet page derives it live: a rostered repo with no readable usage file **is** the absent row, and `dormant` is read off the member's own declaration.

So: drop the task and the file — sequenced after the fleet page stops reading it (the tail, below).

## Design decisions

1. **Fresh vs past split.** *Fresh* per page load: repo metadata, head sha, the open-issue page, the runs list — all ETag-revalidated (a 304 is free), target **~5 requests warm, all 304s** on the per-repo page. *Past*: one blob read of `.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json`, cached by head sha — **zero requests while `main` is unmoved**. Nothing else reaches back in time over the API.
2. **usage.GENERATED.json v3 stays raw data**, not UI-shaped: per-hour and per-day series with per-item detail preserved, so future UI changes re-render without re-folding. Readers accept v2 (legacy at the door): an absent series renders as a stated gap, never a guessed zero — the #1001 rule.
3. **Freshness provenance**: a `generated` stamp in the file, excluded from the worker's unchanged-compare exactly as the fleet file's `generatedAt` already is — so it reads "when the data last moved" and a quiet repo still opens no PR. The head-commit date the page already holds is the upper bound beside it.
4. **usage-fold goes hourly, gated on movement** — signals `commits` + `conversationLogs` + runs movement; a quiet hour declines. The REST-read families stay incremental past their watermarks; day recomputes stay local-git and free.
5. **Mode is structural, no new config key**: a declaration with a roster source (`owner` or legacy `rosterFile`) is a **fleet-dashboard** deployment, anything else is a **repo-dashboard** one; `build-site.mjs` mounts that landing. Nothing to ask at adoption, nothing to misconfigure.
6. **Fleet roster = live enumeration as the viewer**: config `owner` (+ existing `exclude`), membership = a readable `.claudinite-checks.json` at head (sha-cached, so the probe is amortized). This also honors the standing "no repo list exists anywhere in canon code" decision. Fallback if enumeration proves too costly at fleet size: a slim `roster.GENERATED.json` from a Shepherd fleet task (the sanctioned daily auto-merged GENERATED-file shape) — not built unless measurement says so.

## Phase 0 — out-of-band, human

- [x] Enable **Pages, source "GitHub Actions", on ClaudiniteCanary** — the one repository setting no Action can flip. The adoption run files its own handover issue there with the link; while off, only the deploy job fails. (Shepherd already deploys, so its setting is expected on — verified as an execution step, promoted here only if it turns out off.)

Sign-in for the fleet deployment is already tracked in #996 / #942 / #1003 and blocks nothing here — the token box works today.

## The stack — all code, one review pass, merged base-first

- [x] **PR 1 — usage-fold v3** (the data plane; everything downstream renders from it)
  - **`hours` tier**, rolling ~72h keyed by UTC hour: counts of scheduler runs / executor runs / agentic runs, plus raw per-run entries (task ids evaluated / executed, which dispatched an agent, conclusion) so the UI can build hover detail. Folded from the Actions runs listing + the run records, incremental past `runsFoldedThrough`. This is the queue-era successor to the dead `tasks` census — closes #994.
  - **day-row additions**: `queue` — closed work items per task × outcome, appended past a watermark (settled data, never re-read); `ruleTokens` — sessions seen + rule tokens summed, parsed from the session-start summary line the capture logs already carry; `linesCommitted` — local git, free; `releases` — tags, one cheap read.
  - **aspirational, resolved inside this PR**: per-session token spend — probe the capture JSONL for usage records; carried if present, otherwise the README names it absent (a stated gap, not an approximation).
  - `generated` stamp per decision 3; `frequency: 'hourly'` + movement precondition per decision 4; README rewritten.
  - Exit: fold runs green on this repo's own logs; a v2 file re-folds to v3 without loss; a quiet-hour run declines.
- [x] **PR 2 — per-repo page redesign**
  - **At-a-glance tiles**: stars, CI health, waiting-on-a-person minutes (the fleet's flat-rate constant, same published assumption note), "N parked for approval / M for a decision" (the park-kind split `summariseMember` already makes, reused per-repo), open PRs + issues, engine/pack drift vs `canonRepo` (reads *unknown* when unset — never guessed).
  - **One work table** replacing the tasks and queue tables: three views — **stuck / pending / all** — over the union of declared tasks and their items, with view-dependent columns; transitions FLIP-animated (rows enter/leave, columns slide; hand-rolled, the pack keeps zero dependencies). Blocked/parked rows always on top; healthy rows collapsed behind **show all**.
  - **Task execution summary**: per-day stacked outcome bars (the fleet's shape), from the usage `queue` series, today's partial day topped up from the live issue page already fetched.
  - **Scheduler-runs panel condensed to a 48h hourly stacked graph** — scheduler / executor / agentic per hour, hover naming the tasks evaluated / executed / agentic — from the usage `hours` tier, the freshest hours topped up from the runs list already fetched.
  - **Growth block, centrally placed**: 30-day graph, dual axes — rule tokens added to sessions per day, checks executed per day — plus the aspirational series where the file carries them.
  - Exit: cold/warm request counts measured and stated in the README, warm within the ~5-request target.
- [x] **PR 3 — fleet page from member usage files**
  - Member rows and the activity/growth panels render from each member's usage file (sha-keyed read, zero when unmoved) plus a minimal fresh read per member (ETag'd open-issue page + repo meta), through the existing cache/budget tiers.
  - Roster from `owner` enumeration per decision 6; `rosterFile` still accepted so Shepherd's current declaration keeps working until flipped.

input.title: An absorbed pack's leftover directory collides with its survivor, failing the converged tree's self-test and freezing seven members
input.body:
Seven members have not landed a mount update since ~10 August. Each runs its converge daily, produces an update branch, opens a PR — and the PR is parked `needs-human` with the body:

> **needs-human** — the converged tree FAILED its self-test — the machinery that runs the rules is not intact, so the PR stays open

## Root cause

`engine/pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs:192` canonicalizes a **canon** pack's own declared id through `RENAMED_PACKS`:

```js
...(local ? {} : { id: canonicalPackId(mod.id) }),
```

The comment above it states the case it was written for: a directory *renamed* by a migration record while the `pack.mjs` inside still carries the old id. In a rename there is only ever **one** directory, so canonicalizing its id is safe.

`RENAMED_PACKS` also carries **absorptions** (#1057, #1079), which are a different shape — the absorbed pack's directory and its survivor's directory both exist:

```js
'chrome-extension-release': 'chrome-extension',
'github-actions': 'git-github',
```

When a member's mount holds both, discovery reads `packs/chrome-extension-release/pack.mjs` (id `chrome-extension-release`), canonicalizes it to `chrome-extension`, and collides with the real `chrome-extension` pack. Both packs are dropped and an error is raised — with the tell-tale message naming one source twice:

```
pack id "chrome-extension" is declared twice — by the canon and the canon
pack id "git-github" is declared twice — by the canon and the canon
```

That fails the `pack-manifests` probe, so the converged tree fails its self-test and the converge parks the PR.

## Why it is a deadlock, and why it started on 10 August

The absorbed directory is only ever removed from a member's mount by a converge that lands. The converge cannot land, because the tree it delivers fails the self-test. So the member re-derives the same broken tree every day, forever.

It began when the engine carrying the `canonicalPackId(mod.id)` line started being delivered — members' current `main` still runs the older engine, which does not canonicalize a canon pack's own id, so **`main` self-tests clean** while the branch fails. That is exactly why the members look healthy: green scheduler runs, green `main`, an update branch every cycle, nothing merging.

## Evidence

Reproduced directly against `missingbulb/CrosswordChat` PR #249's head:

```
$ node .claudinite/shared/engine/selftest.mjs      # the branch (engine 60820.1)
Claudinite self-test: 1 of 6 probes FAILED — pack-manifests
  - pack-manifests: 2 pack(s) failed to load or validate — first: pack id
    "chrome-extension" is declared twice — by the canon and the canon

$ node .claudinite/shared/engine/selftest.mjs      # the same repo's main (engine 4)
Claudinite self-test: 6 probes passed.
```

The presence of an absorbed pack directory predicts the stall exactly, 10/10 across the fleet:

| member | absorbed dirs in mount | state |
|---|---|---|
| CrosswordChat | `chrome-extension-release`, `github-actions` | stuck |
| GoogleCalendarEventCreator | `chrome-extension-release`, `github-actions` | stuck |
| TLDR | `chrome-extension-release`, `github-actions` | stuck |
| EdFringeNow | `github-actions` | stuck |
| LaughCounter | `github-actions` | stuck |
| ClaudiniteWebsite | `github-actions` | stuck |
| MissingBulbWebsite | `github-actions` | stuck |
| VascularColoring | — | converged today |
| ShoutsAndWhispers | — | converged today |
| WIP | — | converged today |

Parked PRs: CrosswordChat#249, LaughCounter#251, ClaudiniteWebsite#237, MissingBulbWebsite#201, plus the equivalents on EdFringeNow, GoogleCalendarEventCreator and TLDR.

Two claims worth correcting for anyone reading the earlier diagnosis: the pinned `claudinite.ref` (`631a067f`) is identical on the **healthy** members too, so it discriminates nothing; and the large `claudinite/*` branch counts (42 and 51) are mostly `usage-fold/*` and are just as high on healthy members.

## The fix

Canonicalize a canon pack's own id **only when no other canon pack already carries that id literally**. That keeps the rename case working (one directory, no survivor present, so it is canonicalized as before) and makes the absorption case resolve to the survivor, dropping the superseded leftover instead of taking both packs down with it.

The fix reaches the frozen members without any per-repo hand-running: the self-test runs against the **converged tree**, so the next converge vendors the fixed `pack-registry.mjs` and the probe passes.

## Why it matters

It is the last open box on #1158 — "every folding member's usage file reads `version: 3`". These seven read v2 because they never received the `claudinite-growth` version that folds v3. Readers accept v2 so nothing is broken for a user, but the members are ~11 days behind on everything the canon has shipped.

input.body:
Closes #1186

Seven members have not landed a mount update since ~10 August. Each runs its converge daily, opens a PR, and the PR is parked:

> **needs-human** — the converged tree FAILED its self-test — the machinery that runs the rules is not intact

## The bug

`RENAMED_PACKS` holds two shapes that read identically in the map:

| shape | what the tree holds |
|---|---|
| **rename** (`core` → `claudinite-lifecycle`) | one directory — the migration record's `aliases` moves it |
| **absorption** (`github-actions` → `git-github`, #1057/#1079) | **both** directories — there is no record, and the pack flow "never removes a tree that has stopped being declared" (its own words, `2026-08-19-pack-renames/migration.mjs`) |

`scanPackDir` canonicalized a canon pack's own id from the map alone. Correct for a rename; for an absorption it put two live directories on one id, so the collision guard dropped **both**:

```
pack id "chrome-extension" is declared twice — by the canon and the canon
pack id "git-github" is declared twice — by the canon and the canon
```

That fails the `pack-manifests` probe → the converged tree fails its self-test → the converge parks its own PR. The leftover directory is only ever removed by a converge that lands, so the member re-derives the same broken tree every day. A closed loop.

It surfaced on 10 August because members' current `main` runs the older engine, which does not canonicalize a canon pack's own id — so `main` self-tests clean while the branch fails, which is why the members look healthy: green runs, green `main`, nothing merging.

## The change

The map can't distinguish the two shapes, but the tree can. The id is now resolved once the whole canon scan is known: an absorbed leftover whose survivor is present keeps its own id and goes inert — what an id nothing declares is meant to do. A member still declaring the absorbed spelling is unaffected, since the declaration side resolves onto the survivor, which is live.

## Verification

Against `missingbulb/CrosswordChat`#249's **actual head**, with only this change vendored in:

```
before   Claudinite self-test: 1 of 6 probes FAILED — pack-manifests
         2 pack(s) failed to load or validate
after    Claudinite self-test: 6 probes passed.          (discoverPacks: 0 errors)
```

- New `engine-tests/pack_loader/renamed-packs.test.mjs` — 4 tests covering both shapes and the no-duplicates property; written first and watched fail on the missing export.
- Full suite: 2503 pass, 1 fail — `engine-pack-lane-shims`, which is the shallow-clone guard firing on this session's own checkout (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` → `true`). It walks pack history and touches nothing in this diff.
- `check_the_work` and `check_the_world`: 0 blocking.

**This reaches the frozen members with no per-repo hand-running** — the self-test runs against the converged tree, so the next converge vendors the fixed loader and the probe passes.

## Folders touched

**`engine/pack_loader/`** — `renamed-packs.mjs` gains `canonicalPackIdAmong`, which only maps an id forward when the target isn't already present in the tree; `pack-registry.mjs` carries each canon pack's raw id through `scanPackDir` and re-resolves the whole set in `discoverPacks`, where the full tree is known.

## Not in this change

The absorbed leftovers stay on disk as inert, undeclared trees — harmless now, but dead weight that nothing prunes. Worth its own issue (the fix is a migration record that *deletes* rather than moves, since the survivor's directory already exists); deliberately kept out of the change that unfreezes the fleet.

description: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
---

# /do-later — defer a change into a chained request run

The owner has spotted a change that should happen **after** the work in front of
them. Doing it now derails the session; an ordinary issue waits for somebody to
remember it. This files it as an **ad-hoc request** (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §16):
an issue the queue picks up on its own, held behind what is still in flight.

You are filing work, not doing it. Touch no source file, open no branch.

## What you write

**One issue, well defined.** The run that implements it will never see this
conversation — the issue body is the whole brief. State the change, the files or
surfaces it touches if you know them, what "done" looks like, and anything the
owner ruled out. Size it to its idea; a rename is a sentence.

Give the body these two lines, verbatim in this spelling — the scheduler run reads the
first one:

```
Blocked-by: #<what this waits on>
```

name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.
